column1: # Declared platform gaps for the dev-environment tool tier.
# Read by tools/dev_env_platform_coverage.nim. Every (package, platform) cell
# that no realization covers must have a row here, and the state has to be
#   upstream-none  Upstream publishes no asset for that platform. A fact
#                  about the world. It changes when upstream ships one.
#   not-pinned     Upstream publishes one and this catalog has not pinned
#                  it. Work, and the reason should say what the asset is so
#                  the next person does not have to go looking.
# The reasons below were checked against upstream release listings at the
# versions this catalog pins, not inferred from the recipe's own prose.
# The header line that follows is required verbatim, tabs included.

column5: reason

rust-1.92.0-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.tar.xz exists on static.rust-lang.org and carries the clippy component; rustc, cargo and rustfmt reach this platform through their scoop slices and clippy has none, so the gap is one missing slice rather than a missing asset.
mvdan/sh v3.12.0 publishes shfmt_v3.12.0_windows_386.exe and _windows_amd64.exe and no arm64 Windows asset.

jqlang/jq jq-1.7.1 publishes jq-win64.exe and jq-windows-amd64.exe; its only other Windows asset is i386. Upstream added a windows-arm64 asset in 1.8.x, which is a version bump rather than a missing pin.
WinLibs builds the MinGW-w64 toolchain for i686 and x86_64 Windows hosts only.

This package IS the WinLibs Windows-hosted toolchain. A MinGW-w64 cross-compiler hosted on Linux exists, but it is a different upstream, a different layout and a different package; claiming this one covers it would make `mingw-gcc` mean two things.
Same as linux-x86_64: WinLibs hosts on Windows only.

The electron-builder-binaries wix payload is architecture-neutral: the WiX 3.x tools are x86 PE binaries, and electron-builder's MsiTarget forces wixArch to x64 even when targeting arm64. So the same archive would serve, but the slice qualifies itself `cpu = "x86_64"` and nothing has run it on an arm64 Windows host, so the catalog does not offer what it has not seen work.
